12220dbf9554c598a6d60429015d4f091ebd4afb.summary: Yonhap reports that a joint government-private investigation into SK Telecom's large-scale data breach was extended to the servers of KT Corp. and LG Uplus. Per industry sources, no hacking traces had been found on those servers yet. Interim findings from a media briefing cite 25 malware variants on 23 SK Telecom servers: 24 variants of BPFDoor and one of WebCell. Two affected servers were used as temporary storage for personal data, including names, birthdates, phone numbers, email addresses and IMEI data. SK Telecom discovered the breach on April 18.

1269e37e6a2c2ba3c89a762b1d250a33e6ef30ae.summary: FireEye's April 2017 report describes FIN7, a financially motivated group that many vendors call Carbanak Group. FIN7 ran spear phishing campaigns against restaurant chains, hospitality and financial service organizations. Lures in DOCX and RTF files use embedded hidden LNK shortcuts and VBScript run through mshta.exe to drop a Cobalt Strike stager and the HALFBAKED backdoor. Persistence uses scheduled tasks and a registry auto-start. FIN7 called victim stores to walk staff through infection. FireEye ran a Community Protection Event on April 12 to protect affected clients.

120cbc9526ac2273bc9be8e0092553fa87779154.summary: An overview of five JavaScript-based Windows malware strains: VJw0rm, WSHRat, STRRAT, the BlackByte ransomware and a Carbanak/FIN7 JavaScript backdoor. It covers how each spreads, mostly through malicious email attachments, and what each does after running. The review is described as higher-level rather than in-depth. Caveats include an estimate that script-based attacks may be 40 percent or more of all cyberattacks, an estimated $1 billion in losses attributed to Carbanak/FIN7, and a link between Houdini/WSHRat and an aviation-industry espionage campaign.
